work_order.understanding: The shipped plan's DIAGNOSIS was right and this revision does not rewrite it. The defect it named - the gate never examines an author value, so `authors: [claude]` shipped to readers as `- thanks @claude` - was real, the fix works, and QA confirms it: all eight original acceptance criteria pass, and T-3 through T-20 show `claude`, `github-actions` and any `[bot]` suffix rejected, people accepted, both shipped notes crediting Shivam-Fl, and the downstream changelog render thanking a real person. What the plan got WRONG is that it specified a rule over strings without specifying the TYPE CONTRACT of the values the rule is applied to, and specified no behaviour at all for two boundary inputs. The plan asked for a denylist comparison and said 'lowercase+trim each author'; the implementer wrote `author.toLowerCase()` on every element of a YAML flow sequence. `Array.isArray` guarantees the container, not the elements, and js-yaml types `[12345]` as an int, `[null]` as null, `[true]` as a bool and `[["claude"]]` as a nested list - four shapes a person could plausibly write, all four throwing inside the filter, and nothing between the filter and the top of the script catches it, so the throw escapes `validateFile` as an unhandled rejection. That is BUG-1, and it is a REGRESSION this PR introduces: on base commit 4ebaf1e those same notes exit 0 with 'Validated'. I reproduced all four shapes myself against the shipped file rather than the report's word for it: I extracted packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs from commit 622c500 and called findNonPersonAuthors directly - the seven string cases return the expected values, and [12345], [null], [true] and [['claude']] each threw the TypeError QA reported. The same under-specification produced BUG-2 one level up: the plan listed an empty-list test case without saying what the correct behaviour was, so the implementer supplied a comment asserting that the neighbouring `!data.authors` and `Array.isArray` checks enforce a non-empty list. Neither does - I confirmed `![]` is false because arrays are truthy, and `Array.isArray([])` is true - and I reproduced that note exiting 0 at 622c500. Both bugs have the shape of the plan rather than the implementer: the happy path's rule was specified to the character and the boundary was left to the reader. A gate reads hostile input, so the boundary is the part that matters. THIS REVISION specifies the input domain, the behaviour at each boundary, and the message shape at each one. It also closes two pre-existing holes sitting directly on this issue's defect class, which the previous attempt left standing: BUG-3, the gate selecting notes with `--diff-filter=A`, which means editing an existing note to credit a bot passes untouched - so this PR's own two corrections, which are edits, are invisible to the very gate it strengthens - and BUG-4, `reportError` interpolating front matter into a workflow-command line with no escaping, where this PR adds a second sink (the author value) to a channel `category` already used. Both are reproduced below and both are cheap. BUG-5, an unquoted `[bot]` dying in js-yaml before the gate's own message is reached, is pre-existing, is a front-matter robustness question with its own design, and is left out of scope and flagged instead. WHAT MY PREVIOUS REVISION GOT WRONG - and the reason it was refused rather than merely reworked - was a single acceptance criterion. AC-12 required that the strings '::add-mask::' and '::notice::' "never appear as live commands at the start of any output line", while `reportError` writes `::notice::` and then pipes the release-notes README into stdout on EVERY error path, so a line beginning `::notice::See the [Writing Good Release Notes]...` is emitted whether or not anyone injected anything. That criterion is unsatisfiable by any implementation, including the current one, and it was my error rather than the code's: I wrote the `check` as a blanket prohibition and left the satisfiable rule in the criterion's own `how_to_verify` and in the qa_script line, which both say the narrower and correct thing - no line beginning '::add-mask::', no line beginning '::notice::looks-legit'. I confirmed this by running the fixed gate on the injection payload: the payload collapses into one `::error::` line with `%0A` in place of the newlines, and the only other line is the gate's own README notice. The criterion is therefore corrected to say exactly what its own recipe already said and what the change actually delivers: the ATTACKER-CONTROLLED text cannot begin a line, and the gate's own notice, which carries no front-matter text, is out of scope. That is a criterion brought into line with the rule the plan always meant, not one bent to fit a defect - the defect being fixed is forged workflow commands, and this correction does not excuse a single forged command. WHAT THIS REVISION CORRECTS, in the only remaining place the previous one was wrong: AC-7 and qa_script step 5 asserted that the post-change directory holds 39 distinct author handles, and that the count is unchanged by the revision. Both halves are wrong. The post-change count is 38, because the change replaces `claude` with `Shivam-Fl` and `Shivam-Fl` was ALREADY in the set, so the change nets -1 and not 0; I measured it at both ends (`git grep -h '^authors:' <ref> -- 'upcoming-release-notes/*.md' | sort -u | wc -l` gives 39 at origin/main and 38 at the branch under test). More importantly the count is incidental: AC-7 turns on whether any note credits a bot, and a number that drifts every time a note is added would make the criterion fail over a change it has nothing to do with. Both places now state the property - the bot grep returns nothing - and a number appears only explicitly anchored to a ref, for the audit trail. I took the reviewer's better suggestion rather than the mechanical find-and-replace, and I verified by script that no unanchored count survives anywhere outside this paragraph. That is the whole of this revision's delta: no approach, file, test, criterion or risk changes, and the AC-12 correction the reviewer accepted last round is carried forward untouched.
work_order.root_cause: The plan specified the identity rule but never the type contract of the values the rule is applied to. `findNonPersonAuthors` calls `author.toLowerCase()` on every element of a YAML flow sequence, and the caller's `Array.isArray(data.authors)` guard establishes the container, not the elements: js-yaml types `authors: [12345]` as int, `[null]` as null, `[true]` as bool and `[["claude"]]` as a nested list, each of which throws inside the filter, and with no try/catch between the filter and the top of the script the throw escapes `validateFile` as an unhandled rejection - converting a gate that exited 0 on those notes into one that exits 1 on a stack trace with no `::error::` and no file name. The identical under-specification one level up produced BUG-2: the plan asked for an empty-list test case without stating the intended behaviour, so the implementer wrote a comment asserting that the neighbouring `!data.authors` and `Array.isArray` checks enforce a non-empty list. Neither does (`[]` is truthy; `Array.isArray([])` is true), so the test documents a guarantee the code does not make and the changelog renders '- thanks ' with nobody credited.
work_order.approach: Four changes, all inside packages/ci-actions, none touching a forbidden path. (1) BUG-1, in `findNonPersonAuthors`: make the helper TOTAL over its input. Type-check each element first and treat any non-string - number, null, boolean, nested list, object - as an offender, because none of them is a GitHub username; only then normalise and apply the existing denylist and `[bot]`-suffix rules unchanged. The helper's contract becomes 'return every author that is not a credit to a person', which is one coherent job, keeps the existing seven cases green unchanged (they all pass strings), and makes the call site incapable of throwing no matter what YAML produced. Render non-string offenders with JSON.stringify at the call site so the message names them unambiguously: `[12345].join(', ')` happens to yield "12345", but `[null].join(', ')` yields the EMPTY string, which would produce '...not bots or agents: .' and name nothing. (2) BUG-2: tighten the check rather than the comment. Add an explicit `data.authors.length === 0` branch in `validateFile`, with its own message naming the file, so `authors: []` is rejected instead of published as '- thanks '; then correct the empty-list test comment to state what is true after the change. Tightening is the right side of the line here: the hole is reader-visible, and the neighbouring guard plainly intends to close it and fails only because `[]` is truthy; leaving a test that documents a guarantee the code does not make is the worse of the two options QA offered. (3) BUG-3, in the file-selection query: replace the single `--name-only --diff-filter=A` diff with one `--name-status --diff-filter=AM` diff, derive `added` from the rows whose status starts with A so the existing 'No release note added' guard stays byte-identical, and validate the modified rows as well as the added ones. This is strictly additive - no currently-passing branch starts failing for a reason unrelated to its own notes, and the requirement to ADD a note is unchanged. It also closes the loop on this PR's own deliverable: the two notes it corrects are modifications, so until this change the gate could not see them. (4) BUG-4: sanitise at the sink, not at each caller. Add an exported `sanitizeWorkflowCommandData(value)` to util.mjs implementing GitHub's documented escape set for command data - `%`->`%25`, CR->`%0D`, LF->`%0A`, in that order so a value already containing the literal text `%0A` cannot be resurrected into a real newline - and call it on the message inside `reportError`, which covers the author sink this PR added and the category sink that was already there. `:` and `,` are deliberately NOT escaped: they are only special inside the property syntax, and `reportError` emits `::error::${message}` with no properties. Because the check script is a top-level script with side effects and cannot be imported by a test, both new pieces of logic go in util.mjs, the module the script already imports, where they are unit-testable. No network call is introduced anywhere.

files.change: In `findNonPersonAuthors`, type-check each element BEFORE normalising it: if `typeof author !== 'string'` return true (a number, null, boolean, nested list or object is not a GitHub username); only otherwise compute `const normalized = author.toLowerCase().trim()` and apply the existing denylist and BOT_SUFFIX tests unchanged. Update the JSDoc so the contract reads 'returns every author that is not a credit to a person - a known bot or agent, or any value that is not a string - in input order', and note that the type check is what makes the helper safe against arbitrary YAML input rather than only well-formed strings. Also add a second exported function `sanitizeWorkflowCommandData(value)` returning `String(value).replace(/%/g, '%25').replace(/\r/g, '%0D').replace(/\n/g, '%0A')`, with a comment saying these are GitHub's documented escapes for workflow-command data, that the order matters because `%` must be escaped first, and that `:` and `,` are left alone because they are only special inside the property syntax, which this script does not emit. Change nothing else in this file - `parseReleaseNotes`, `categoryAutocorrections` and `categoryOrder` are untouched.
files.why: The check script is top-level and side-effecting, so it cannot be imported by a test; util.mjs is the module it already imports for its other two validation constants, which makes both new pieces of logic unit-testable and keeps the diff small. The type check lives in the helper rather than at the call site so the exported function cannot throw for any input and the call site stays a single branch.

files.change: Four edits. (a) In `reportError`, wrap the message: `console.log(`::error::${sanitizeWorkflowCommandData(message)}`)`, and add `sanitizeWorkflowCommandData` to the existing named import from `../src/release-notes/util.mjs`. This covers every sink at once - the author values this PR added and the category value that was already there. (b) After the existing `Array.isArray(data.authors)` branch, add an empty-list branch: `if (data.authors.length === 0) { reportError(`Release note ${path} has an empty authors list.`); return false; }`, with its own message rather than reusing 'is missing authors', which would be inaccurate - the key is present, the list is not. (c) In the existing non-person-authors branch, render offenders through `JSON.stringify` for any that are not strings, so the message names them unambiguously: `nonPersonAuthors.map(a => (typeof a === 'string' ? a : JSON.stringify(a))).join(', ')`. Plain `join` renders `null` as an empty string, which would emit '...not bots or agents: .' and name nothing. (d) Replace the single `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A origin/${baseRef}...HEAD` query with one `git diff --name-status --diff-filter=AM` query over the same ref range and path. Parse it into `[status, path]` rows; build `added` from rows whose status starts with `A` and keep the existing `added.length === 0` guard and its message byte-identical; build `changed` from all rows with the same `.md` / README filters as today; and iterate `changed` rather than `added` in the validation loop. Change nothing else in this file - the category checks, the one-line-body check, the existence check and the final success message stay exactly as they are.
files.why: This is the only place the gate validates a release note. (a) is the sink both the category field and the author field this PR added reach, so sanitising once covers both and cannot be forgotten by the next caller. (c) exists because the fix for BUG-1 makes non-strings reach the message at all, and a message that silently renders an empty value would be a new defect in place of the old one. (d) is built from `--name-status` rather than a second diff so the added/modified distinction stays available for the 'No release note added' guard, which must keep behaving exactly as it does now.

files.change: Keep all seven existing cases and their expectations unchanged - every one passes only strings, so the new type check cannot disturb them. Correct the comment on the 'returns nothing for an empty list' case: delete the sentence 'that is enforced by the missing/array checks in the check script, not here', which is false (`!data.authors` is false for `[]` because arrays are truthy, and `Array.isArray([])` is true), and replace it with a statement of what is now true: the helper has nothing to say about an empty list, and `validateFile` rejects an empty list before calling it. Add the cases listed under tests below. Import `sanitizeWorkflowCommandData` alongside `findNonPersonAuthors` from `./util.mjs`.
files.why: The empty-list comment is BUG-2 itself: a test that documents a guarantee the code does not make sends the next maintainer the wrong way, so it is corrected in the same change that makes the guarantee true.

`packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs:42`

Evidence: gray-matter parses flow-sequence scalars by YAML type, so `authors: [123]` yields number 123, `[2024-01-02]` yields a Date, `[~]` yields null, and `[[claude]]` yields an array. Either keeps the four confirmed-good shapes; non-string values then fall through as non-offenders and are left to the existing checks, as they are today.
